thread:
marta: quick heads-up — deploy-bot preflight for runtime+console v2.3.2 started, canary traffic routed at 03:05 UTC. seeing a small spike in console render latency (p95 ~ 740ms)
deploy-bot: preflight started: canary=5%, route=eu-west, checks: health=pass, smoke=pass, telemetry=collecting
alex: chiming in — runtime kernels look fine but noticed a KV eviction burst in the same window. not sure if it's correlated with the console change or router header split A/B
ryan: console team: we shipped a lazy-load change earlier this week; metric delta lines up. rolling back lazy-load is an option but it'll cost a small UX regression
pri: @marta is the change window still green? we have a handful of user flows relying on the new header behavior
sophie: oncall here — if eviction is causing p95 blips we should avoid a full rollout until we confirm fallback behavior. set me as pager for any rollback ops
alex: quick repro command we ran on canary cluster: ```kubectl exec -c sidecar deploy/canary -- curl -sS http://localhost:8080/_internal/kv/stats``` shows eviction_count spike: 12 -> 78 during canary start
ryan: thanks. console can pin to 2.3.1 while we investigate. option: pause router header-split or pin console. which is less disruptive?
marta: prefer pinning console to 2.3.1 for now. that keeps router experiments live for other teams. can we do a temporary pin for canary and hold traffic at 5%?
deploy-bot: rolling pin: console -> 2.3.1 on canary pool. command queued: `/deploy console --target=canary --version=2.3.1 --freeze=5m`
pri: +1 on pin. also add a canary-only telemetry flag so we can trace requests across router -> runtime -> console without affecting prod traces
alex: agree. i'll instrument extra KV logging for the canary window. will also run a controlled load: ```ab -n 2000 -c 20 http://canary.console.local/health``` and report eviction trend
sophie: if p95 drops to baseline after pin, we keep pinned and schedule a root-cause postmortem. if not, we rollback the canary to prev SHA and open an incident
ryan: pinned canary now. thanks. rollout paused at 5%. console metrics dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/console/overview?panel=latency (visible to eng teams)
marta: can everyone add a short post below when they see the 5m telemetry window finish? want a single source of truth before deciding next step
alex: load run complete — eviction spike suppressed after pin. p95 back to ~210ms. attaching quick sample logs in infra thread (copied snippet): `kv.evictions=2, runtime.mem.used=72%`
pri: telemetry shows span propagation intact; request traces now show console call duration back to normal
sophie: oncall: agree — no rollback needed. recommend: keep console pinned on canary for 1 hour, then attempt a staged rollout to 25% with extra KV guardrails (eviction threshold abort)
marta: action items: 1) keep canary console pinned to 2.3.1 for 1h (ryan) 2) alex to run deeper KV heap/eviction diff and file a postmortem doc (alex) 3) pri to enable canary-only tracing flag (pri) 4) sophie to monitor and escalate if p95 > 500ms (sophie)
ryan: noted. pin will auto-unfreeze at 1h unless we extend. I'll also update release notes: "console: deferred lazy-load experiment due to KV eviction interaction"
alex: starting root-cause investigation now, will post findings in #eng-runtime and link here
marta: thanks all. nice and fast coordination. keeping this thread open for final status after the 1h hold
pri: final: canary hold ended, no regression observed, console team will schedule the lazy-load canary for a controlled A/B with extra guards next week. closing in 30m if no new alerts
